questions.analysis_html: \begin{aligned}& \text{先证明极限存在，由}0<x_{1}<3 \text{知}x_{1},3-x_{1} \text{均为正数，故} \\& \quad0<x_{2}=\sqrt{x_{1}(3-x_{1})}\leq \frac{1}{2}(x_{1}+3-x_{1})=\frac{3}{2}.\\& \quad \text{设}0<x_{k}\leq \frac{3}{2}(k>1)\text{，则}0<x_{k+1}=\sqrt{x_{k}(3-x_{k})}\leq \frac{1}{2}(x_{k}+3-x_{k})=\frac{3}{2}.\\& \quad \text{由数学归纳法知，对任意正整数}n>1 \text{均有}0<x_{k}\leq \frac{3}{2}\text{，因而数列}\{x_{n}\}\text{有界}.\\& \quad \text{又当}n>1 \text{时，}x_{n+1}-x_{n}=\sqrt{x_{n}(3-x_{n})}-x_{n}=\sqrt{x_{n}}(\sqrt{3-x_{n}}-\sqrt{x_{n}})=\frac{\sqrt{x_{n}}(3-2x_{n})}{\sqrt{3-x_{n}}+\sqrt{x_{n}}}\geq 0\text{，}\\& \quad \text{因而有}x_{n+1}\geq x_{n}(n>1)\text{，即数列}\{x_{n}\}\text{单调增加}.\\& \quad \text{由单调有界数列必有极限知}\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}x_{n}\text{存在.设}\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}x_{n}=a\text{，在}x_{n+1}=\sqrt{x_{n}(3-x_{n})}\text{两边取极限，得}a=\sqrt{a(3-a)}\text{，解之得}a=\frac{3}{2},a=0\text{（舍去）.故}\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}x_{n}=\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}

questions.analysis_html: \begin{array}{l} \lim\limits_{x \to 0} \left( \dfrac{a^{x}+b^{x}+c^{x}}{3} \right)^{\frac{1}{x}} = \lim\limits_{x \to 0} \left( 1 + \dfrac{a^{x}+b^{x}+c^{x}-3}{3} \right)^{\frac{3}{a^{x}+b^{x}+c^{x}-3}-\dfrac{a^{x}+b^{x}+c^{x}-3}{3x}}, \text{因为} \\ \lim\limits_{x \to 0} \left( 1 + \dfrac{a^{x}+b^{x}+c^{x}-3}{3} \right)^{\frac{3}{a^{x}+b^{x}+c^{x}-3}} = e. \\ \lim\limits_{x \to 0} \dfrac{a^{x}+b^{x}+c^{x}-3}{3x} = \frac{1}{3} \lim\limits_{x \to 0} \left( \dfrac{a^{x}-1}{x} + \dfrac{b^{x}-1}{x} + \dfrac{c^{x}-1}{x} \right) \\ = \frac{1}{3} \left[ \ln a \lim\limits_{t \to 0} \dfrac{1}{\ln{(1+t)}} + \ln b \lim\limits_{u \to 0} \dfrac{1}{\ln{(1+u)}} + c \lim\limits_{v \to 0} \dfrac{1}{\ln{(1+v)}} \right]^{v} \\ = \frac{1}{3} (\ln a + \ln b + \ln c) = \ln \sqrt[3]{abc} \\ \text{所以} \quad \lim\limits_{x \to 0} \left( \dfrac{a^{x}+b^{x}+c^{x}}{3} \right)^{\frac{1}{x}} = e^{\ln \sqrt[3]{abc}} = \sqrt[3]{abc}. \text{㠠} \\ \text{提示：求极限过程中作了变换} a^{x}-1 = t, b^{x}-1 = u, c^{x}-1 = v. \text{㠠} \end{array}

questions.analysis_html: \begin{aligned}&\lim_{x \rightarrow 0} \left[ \frac{1}{x} - \frac{1}{\ln \left( 1+x \right)} \right] = \lim_{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\ln \left( 1+x \right)-x}{x \ln \left( 1+x \right)} = \lim_{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\ln \left( 1+x \right)-x}{x \cdot x} \\&= \lim_{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{\frac{1}{1+x}-1}{2x} = \lim_{x \rightarrow 0} \frac{x}{2x \left( 1+x \right)} = \frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
